title: Freeze the assessment before changing control
diagram_spec: Three parallel evidence tracks: readings and trust flags; switch states and topology; linear model and noise assumptions. A common vertical cut freezes one assessment packet. Changed input means a new assessment. Unresolved trust means HOLD. Original teaching diagram, not an implemented authentication system.
points: An unusual reading starts an investigation. It does not identify an attacker.
Keep the readings, trust assumptions, topology and model in the same assessment packet.
caption: Proposed defensive assessment discipline for the four-bus teaching fixture.
note: Set the operator problem: a network estimate suggests that no corrective action is needed, but the provenance of some measurements is unresolved. Before asking for a new control, record the reading set, its time, trust flags, topology, model H, noise scales, operating limits and proposed action. A repeated calculation on changed inputs is a new assessment. The three horizontal tracks make this shared context visible; they do not claim that a hash, an LLM or the workshop code authenticates sensors. In the laboratory, trusted_response returns HOLD and dispatch=false when an independent trusted state is unavailable. A residual alarm may reflect a bad reading, topology or model error, or an adversarial change. It alone identifies none of these causes. The upcoming Hc example is a defensive negative control on synthetic data, not a live-system test.

title: Eight readings describe three unknown angles
diagram_spec: Four-bus loop with reference bus 0 at theta0=0 and three unknown angles at buses 1, 2 and 3. Branch reference arrows 0→1, 1→2, 2→3 and 0→3. Measurement composition: four flows, three injections and one angle, yielding eight rows of H and rank three.
points: The state contains three voltage angles. Eight readings provide five extra consistency checks.
This is a DC model: it does not test voltage magnitudes or reactive power.
caption: Exact topology and measurement count in the supplied four-bus fixture. Arrows define positive flow directions.
note: Bus 0 is the reference, with angle zero. The unknown vector is x=(theta1,theta2,theta3). The four line susceptance coefficients are 10, 8, 10 and 5 for reference branches 01, 12, 23 and 03. The linear measurement matrix stacks four flow rows F, three injection rows B, and an angle-1 row. Its rank is three. Thus m=8 measurements minus rank(H)=3 gives five residual degrees of freedom. The arrows define algebraic reference directions; actual flow can be negative. In this fixed DC approximation, active flow is linear in angle differences. It omits voltage magnitude, reactive power, losses, protection behavior and AC constraints. Do not transfer this result to the distribution-feeder model used in the voltage case. Ask participants which extra measurements provide consistency information beyond the minimum needed to solve for the angles.

title: WLS finds the best common explanation
diagram_spec: An equal-precision scalar illustration: two readings 9 and 11 fit a common estimate 10, leaving residuals -1 and +1. Connect the number-line example to the weighted least-squares objective sum of squared residuals divided by sigma squared. Label the scalar illustration separately from the four-bus run.
points: A residual is a reading minus the value predicted by the estimated state.
WLS gives more weight to a reading with a smaller stated noise scale.
caption: The 9–11 example explains fitting; the network calculation estimates three angles from eight readings.
note: Start with the scalar picture. Two equally precise readings of one quantity are 9 and 11. Choosing 10 leaves residuals -1 and +1; moving the estimate toward either reading increases the total squared mismatch. WLS extends this idea to the network predictions Hx. It minimizes the sum over readings of ((z_j-(Hx)_j)/sigma_j)^2. Here z is the reading vector, H maps angles to expected readings, and sigma_j is the assumed standard deviation of the reading noise. A smaller sigma creates a larger penalty for the same raw mismatch. It expresses the estimator's stated precision model, not a cybersecurity trust judgment. The supplied code solves the full-rank weighted problem numerically using least squares. Flow noise scales are 0.004 p.u., injection noise scales 0.006 p.u., and the angle-1 noise scale is 0.0005 rad. Do not interpret unequal weights as proof that a channel is authentic.

title: A residual alarm checks consistency
diagram_spec: A horizontal J axis places the actual nominal statistic 3.92022 below a red threshold 15.0863. Shade only the upper-tail alarm region. Show eight readings minus rank three gives five degrees of freedom and alpha=1%. Clearly separate a consistency test from sensor authenticity.
points: Nominal J = 3.92022 is below the 15.0863 alarm threshold.
The 1% calibration assumes the correct linear model and the stated independent Gaussian noise.
caption: Upper-tail consistency test with five residual degrees of freedom. A quiet alarm does not establish trustworthy data.
note: The statistic is J=r^T R^-1 r, where r=z-Hxhat and R is the diagonal matrix of the assumed noise variances. Under the stated linear Gaussian model, correct H and covariance, and full column rank, the minimized statistic has m-rank(H)=5 degrees of freedom. The 99th percentile is 15.0862724694; use 15.0863 on the slide. Nominal J is 3.9202216910. Alpha=0.01 is a nominal upper-tail false-alarm probability under those assumptions. It is not a 99% chance that the data are safe, nor the probability that an attacker is present. An isolated +0.08 p.u. change on flow12 produces J=277.4974469045 and an alarm in this seeded run. That is evidence of inconsistency, not an identification of the cause or a guarantee that all coordinated errors will be detected.

title: Coordinated changes can leave the residual unchanged
diagram_spec: Two scalar number lines: readings 9 and 11 with estimate 10, then readings 12 and 14 with estimate 13. The residual pair stays -1,+1. Under the picture, display z'=z+Hc, xhat'=xhat+c, and r'=z+Hc-H(xhat+c)=r. Label this a fixed-model explanation, not an operational attack recipe.
points: If readings and the inferred state move together, their mismatch can stay the same.
The Hc result assumes a known fixed model and access to the required unprotected measurement channels.
caption: Defensive explanation of a classical state-estimation limitation. The scalar picture illustrates the cancellation.
note: Return to the scalar illustration: shifting both readings by three moves their best common estimate by three, while the two residuals remain -1 and +1. The linear network identity is z'=z+Hc, xhat'=xhat+c and r'=r when the same full-rank H and weights are used. Here c is a shift in the inferred angle state; Hc is the corresponding change in model predictions. Liu, Ning and Reiter establish this limitation of residual-based bad-data detection. Their result has specific access and model assumptions; it is not a claim that any attacker can alter every utility state estimate. Protected measurements restrict which changes are possible. The synthetic workshop deliberately supplies a matching coordinated perturbation as a negative control, so it can test whether a residual-only workflow mistakes consistency for trust. We do not discuss targeting real measurement channels. The operator lesson is to seek independent evidence when the trust premise is unresolved, even if the residual test is quiet.

title: A quiet residual can hide a wrong inferred state
points: Isolated bias raises J; the coordinated Hc change leaves J near 3.92.
The right panel uses known synthetic truth to reveal the growing state error.
caption: Actual L8 sweep on the four-bus fixture. The left axis uses a symmetric-log scale; the right panel is an offline audit.
note: Read the panels together. At scale zero both cases start from the same seeded noisy readings. Increasing one isolated flow bias raises the weighted residual and eventually crosses the threshold. The coordinated Hc changes leave J essentially unchanged while their state-error norm grows. At scale one the nominal and coordinated statistics are both 3.92022 to displayed precision, but the coordinated state error is 0.0267799957 rad, versus 0.0002374314 rad for nominal noise. The left panel's symmetric-log scale accommodates small and large statistics. The right panel compares the estimate with the known state supplied by the synthetic experiment. A real operator does not have that exact ground truth as an online test input. This is a negative-control demonstration of a detector limitation, not a statistical field evaluation, attack prevalence estimate or measurement of an LLM's detection capability.

title: Independent trusted readings change the evidence
diagram_spec: Three separately trusted angle readings theta1, theta2 and theta3 directly determine a three-angle state through H_T=I_3. Show rank=3 and measurement count=3, so residual redundancy=0. A separate lower path states that unavailable trusted evidence means HOLD. Explicitly mark trust as supplied externally.
points: The fixture supplies three separately trusted angle readings; authentication is assumed.
Three readings for three angles leave no residual redundancy. J = 0 is not a new detection result.
caption: Exact trusted-recovery assumption: three independent angle channels, with no redundant residual test.
note: The protected recovery uses H_T=I_3 with three angle readings. Each has assumed noise standard deviation 0.00005 rad and a separate seeded noise realization. Because the measurement count and rank are both three, the fit is exactly determined: residual degrees of freedom are zero, the residual is zero up to numerical precision, and the code supplies no chi-square threshold or alarm. The trust argument comes from an external assumption about these channels, not their zero residual. The workshop does not implement sensor authentication, prove channel independence operationally, or ask an LLM to decide authenticity. The trusted_response wrapper returns HOLD when the protected set is unavailable. With the set available, it can return a numerical proposal, still with dispatch=false. In an operational design, the utility would need to justify provenance, independence, time alignment and applicability before using a replacement evidence set.

title: A small QP proposes a limited correction
diagram_spec: Plot the convex effort objective 0.5u^2 against u from 0 to 0.5. Shade the feasible interval beginning at actual optimum u=0.121694 and mark that boundary as the constrained minimum. State that all four predicted branch flows must satisfy their rating minus 0.01 p.u. The control is injection at bus2 balanced at reference bus0.
points: The quadratic program (QP) finds the smallest injection satisfying every predicted branch limit with a 0.01 p.u. margin.
The trusted estimate gives u = 0.121694 p.u.; predicted flow12 becomes 0.170000 p.u.
caption: Scalar convex QP in the fixed DC model. The injection at bus 2 is balanced by reference bus 0.
note: The optimizer chooses one nonnegative flexible injection u at bus 2, balanced by bus 0. The objective 0.5u^2 favors a smaller action. It is a quadratic program because this objective is quadratic while the flow constraints and action bounds are linear. Bounds are 0<=u<=0.5 p.u. Every predicted branch flow must lie between minus and plus its rating less a 0.01 p.u. planning margin. Ratings are [0.35,0.18,0.35,0.35] p.u. for branches 01,12,23,03. Flow changes use g=F B^-1 e2, with g12=-4/7, so increasing u reduces the positive 1-to-2 flow. For this protected noisy estimate the binding constraint is predicted flow12=0.17, producing u=0.1216936673 and objective 0.0074046743. This differs from the 0.1225 noiseless arithmetic example in the longer chapter. The code solves the small QP with SLSQP and independently rechecks finite values, action bounds and all predicted constraints. A failed solve or check produces HOLD.

title: Check the consequences on every branch
points: Using the compromised estimate selects no correction; actual toy flow12 stays at 0.240000 p.u.
Trusted recovery reduces it to 0.170461 p.u., below the 0.180000 p.u. rating.
caption: Offline physical audit of the two decisions. Legend labels identify which estimate selected each action; bars show actual toy-model flows.
note: Both sets of bars are evaluated using the known synthetic state after their respective actions, not the measurement estimates themselves. The action based on the coordinated corrupt estimate is u=0, leaving actual flow12 at 0.24, above its 0.18 rating. The trusted set selects u=0.1216936673. Its predicted flow12 is 0.170000; the independent offline physical audit gives actual flow12=0.1704607616. All four actual branch flows satisfy their physical ratings in this fixed toy network. The 0.01 planning margin accommodates the small protected-noise difference in this run; it is not a general robust uncertainty guarantee. Online, the code checks predicted constraints and finite values. Exact actual-state values are retained for experimental evaluation, not assumed to be an available online measurement or an operational authorization gate. The result demonstrates the value of better evidence plus a constrained solver, without establishing a benefit from an LLM.

title: Exercise: HOLD or propose for operator review?
points: A: J = 3.92022; measurement trust unresolved; no independent trusted replacement.
B: J = 277.497; no trustworthy replacement is available.
C: independent trust assumed; current model; all QP checks pass; u = 0.121694. Choose the next step and name one reason.
caption: Work in pairs. Decide whether the evidence supports progressing an advisory study, not field dispatch.
note: Give participants one minute to read, two minutes to compare decisions with a partner, and one minute to prepare a reason and a next evidence request. Correct answers: A is HOLD in the stated stealth-capable trust scenario; low J alone does not resolve provenance. B is HOLD and investigate the inconsistency; the statistic does not identify an attacker or authorize removal of a channel. C may be PROPOSE for operator review within this fixed DC fixture, because the trust premise is supplied externally and the current-model QP and post-solve checks pass. It is not EXECUTE. For C, all four predicted branch constraints, action bounds and finite checks matter. Expected follow-up questions include whether data are current and aligned, who established trust, whether topology or limits changed, and what operational checks the DC fixture omits. Do not reveal the answers while pairs are discussing.

title: Debrief: consistency, trust and permission differ
points: A and B: HOLD. A quiet residual and an alarm give different evidence, but neither repairs missing trust.
C: propose for review. Passing numerical checks does not authorize an action.
The recovery comes from trusted readings and the constrained solver; no LLM authenticates a sensor.
note: Ask one pair to justify each packet. A passes a residual consistency test but has an unresolved trust premise, so the trusted_response policy holds. B fails the residual test, also without a trustworthy replacement, and holds while the discrepancy is investigated. C can progress to a human review packet after the stated current-model checks. The independent trust premise still needs a real operational justification outside this demonstration. Reinforce three separate questions: do the data fit the model; why should the channels be believed; and who is permitted to act? The three trusted angles have no residual redundancy, so their zero residual supplies no extra authenticity evidence. The comparison does not isolate an LLM detection benefit or prove operational cyber resilience. A useful agent can organize the assessment and report what a numerical tool actually checked, while failing closed when necessary evidence is absent.

title: Give the operator an evidence packet
diagram_spec: A bounded handoff: evidence packet lists current inputs/trust premise, u=0.121694 and every predicted branch check. Arrow to an operator review station with HOLD or further study / candidate for authorized process. A dashed boundary marks any live action outside the fixture. Explicitly label dispatch=false.
points: Show the trust premise, current model, proposed action, checked limits and remaining uncertainty together.
The fixture ends at PROPOSE with dispatch = false. Operator review is a separate decision.
caption: Proposed operator handoff. The classroom response is advisory and has no live control connection.
note: The final packet should let the operator trace a recommendation back to its evidence, rather than accept a confident explanation. Include the current reading and topology versions, who established the trusted-channel premise, the fixed DC scope, u=0.121694, predicted flow12=0.170000, all other predicted branch checks, physical ratings, 0.01 planning margin and any failed or omitted checks. State that the offline 0.170461 actual-flow audit used synthetic truth and is not an online truth oracle. The local trusted_response function sets dispatch=false whether it holds or proposes. Any real deployment would require the utility's authorization, operating procedures and applicable additional engineering checks; these are outside this module. The agent's useful role here is to assemble the correct tool calls, preserve the evidence context, flag missing premises and explain verified results. It must not convert low residuals into trust or numerical feasibility into permission.
